I am writing this review to warn other pet owners about the severe lack of professionalism, administrative dysfunction, and disregard for patient well-being at this practice. I trusted this office with the care of my two dogs for the majority of their lives, and while my experience with the vets themselves were usually always positive, my experience with the office staff was consistently disappointing.

Over the years, the baseline operations here were deeply flawed. Wait times were consistently long even for appointments. Getting through to the office via phone was an ongoing battle. Worse, I routinely had to argue with the front desk staff just to secure refills for life-sustaining medications that my dogs required.

At the end of my time spent with this vet, whenever I expressed concerns regarding my dogs health conditions, my observations were routinely blown off or dismissed with assurances that they were "fine." Due to this persistent lack of clinical advocacy and communication, I ultimately transferred their care to another veterinary practice for the final two years of their lives.

The most egregious display of their unprofessionalism, however, occurred after both of my dogs passed away. Despite thanking the office for the years they did provide care to my dogs, when I applied to adopt a dog from a rescue organization, I listed this vet as a reference since they held the bulk of my dogs' medical history. The office staff explicitly lied to the rescue, claiming I had failed to provide annual care for my animals. Fortunately, I maintain meticulous records and possess two large physical files documenting every single visit, vaccine, and treatment they ever received for the last seven years.

This office operates purely as a business transaction, completely devoid of genuine compassion. For the staff to lie to a rescue organization—thereby trying to block an animal from finding a good home—is shameful. If you view your pets as family and expect accurate record-keeping, open communication, and basic empathy, and a vet office that listens and takes your concerns serious, I strongly urge you to take your business elsewhere.
